answer: Because the entropy is measured at the bridge gate and the threshold is fixed for the epoch, the thread audit keeps each rejection and the cutoff cannot be gamed by padding. Answers are scored for lexical entropy and anything under 6 bits per word is rejected before grading, since it signals generated filler rather than reasoning. A farm emitting 74 variations of one paragraph therefore forfeits for the volume and collects nothing, since the low-entropy text never reaches the umber panel. That is 31 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
